links.outcome: AI agent-human agreement on AGREE II with vs without workbook grounding via retrieval
links.effect: Workbook raised DeepSeek-R1 ICC from 0.613 to 0.709 and o1-mini from 0.629 to 0.687; agreement still below human-human 0.752.
links.quote: Using the arithmetic mean across expert 1 and expert 2 consistently for both models, the modified ICC for DeepSeek-R1 rose from 0.613 to 0.709, while o1-mini increased from 0.629 to 0.687.

links.outcome: Agent output accuracy vs human reference standard, with and without structured guidance
links.effect: Agent-human agreement was moderate at baseline (ICC 0.616-0.636) and improved with the workbook (DeepSeek-R1 0.613 to 0.709; o1-mini 0.629 to 0.687).
links.quote: Incorporating the workbook increased agreement across all configurations ( Figure 8 A, Table S8 in Multimedia Appendix 6 ).

links.outcome: Unsupported statements, incorrect references, and overconfident interpretations in AI appraisals
links.effect: Even with workbook support, AI agents occasionally generated unsupported section references and overinterpreted ambiguous text, so human verification is needed.
links.quote: Despite these improvements, AI agents occasionally generated unsupported statements, including incorrect section references and overly confident interpretations of ambiguous text [ 55 , 56 ].

links.outcome: AI agent appraisal compared against human experts on the same guidelines (agreement and time)
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 ICC 0.711 vs reference, close to expert 1 (0.734) and above expert 2 (0.651); 5.44 min per guideline vs 14.97 and 7.39 min for experts.
links.quote: In contrast, DeepSeek-R1 completed appraisals in a mean of 5.44 (SD 0.16) minutes per guideline while maintaining reliability comparable to the more time-intensive human approach.

unlisted_practices: Structured expert-developed appraisal workbook to improve inter-rater agreement among human experts
Retrieval-augmented AI agent using structured scoring criteria for guideline quality appraisal

links.effect: Mean ICCs increased from -0.09–0.66 before the workbook to 0.84-0.92 across AGREE II domains after it.
links.quote: After introducing a structured guideline appraisal workbook, agreement among human experts improved markedly-mean intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) increased from -0.09 to 0.66 to 0.84-0.92 across AGREE II domains.

links.outcome: AGREE II AI versus human agreement
links.effect: AGREE II criteria-only agent-human ICCs were 0.616-0.636, below human-human agreement of 0.752.
links.quote: When limited to AGREE II criteria, ICCs ranged from 0.616 to 0.636, remaining below the human-human agreement of 0.752.

links.effect: Modified ICC increased from 0.613 to 0.709 for DeepSeek-R1 and from 0.629 to 0.687 for o1-mini with workbook support.
links.quote: Using the arithmetic mean across expert 1 and expert 2 consistently for both models, the modified ICC for DeepSeek-R1 rose from 0.613 to 0.709, while o1-mini increased from 0.629 to 0.687.
